sources.author: Jesse Vincent
sources.bundleNote: Superpowers skills are written to work together — using-superpowers teaches the agent when to reach for the rest — so the full set gets the most out of any one of them.

sources.author: Corey Haines
sources.bundleNote: These skills build on shared context: every one of them reads product-marketing first for your product, audience, and positioning, so install product-marketing alongside whichever you pick.

sources.author: Google Workspace CLI
sources.bundleNote: Many Workspace recipes use the shared gws-shared skill and a service-specific skill. Install the Workspace collection to keep those prerequisites together.

sources.author: OpenAI
sources.bundleNote: OpenAI retired this example repository in favor of openai/plugins. This edition preserves the cited revision.

sources.author: xAI
sources.bundleNote: Internal instructions used by the Grok Build bridge for Claude Code. Install the upstream plugin to use its commands.

sources.author: Agrici Daniel
sources.bundleNote: Some workflows use the Claude SEO plugin’s local checks and reference data. Install the upstream plugin to run those checks.

sources.author: OpenSEO
sources.bundleNote: Live research uses an OpenSEO project and its MCP connection. Self-hosted DataForSEO lookups use your provider account and can incur charges.

sources.author: ScrapeCreators
sources.bundleNote: Running live social research uses a ScrapeCreators API key and credits in your own agent.

sources.author: SEO Machine contributors
sources.bundleNote: Growth Lead can work from the business goals, constraints and metrics you provide.

sources.author: Ryze AI
sources.bundleNote: Live reports use the Ryze MCP connector and authorized data sources such as Google Search Console, GA4 or Google Ads.

sources.author: PostHog
sources.bundleNote: These workflows use PostHog product tools and project data. Some need features such as experiments, heatmaps or AI visibility enabled in your PostHog project.

sources.author: dbt Labs
sources.bundleNote: Warehouse queries and project workflows use your own dbt credentials and permissions.

sources.author: Slidev
sources.bundleNote: The Slidev project documents this presentation skill for Claude Code.

sources.author: Julien Thibeaut
sources.bundleNote: Design engineering guidance from Julien Thibeaut. Improve UI includes the publisher’s OpenAI product manifest.

sources.author: Mirza Iqbal
sources.bundleNote: Includes the submission checklist, rejection guide and review-notes template. The automated audit uses the publisher’s guard and reference data. Check the current Apple and Google policies before submitting.

sources.author: Mirza Iqbal
sources.bundleNote: Includes the portable skill and its twelve reference chapters. The publisher supplies the optional checker scripts and assistant-specific installers.

sources.author: Mirza Iqbal
sources.bundleNote: Running this workflow requires the Hetzner MCP server and your own Hetzner credentials. Review the price before authorizing billable resources.

sources.author: Mirza Iqbal
sources.bundleNote: Includes the workflow map, API conventions and endpoint inventory. The publisher’s checkout contains the full OpenAPI specifications and the Xentral MCP server.

sources.author: Theo Browne
sources.bundleNote: Several tstack skills call each other. Install all nine together for the full workflow. GitHub operations use an authenticated GitHub CLI. Council and Sol Loop require access to other models. Babysit PR includes a Python 3 helper.

sources.author: T3 Code
sources.bundleNote: These contributor workflows use a T3 Code checkout. The publisher provides the app, device and browser panels, video assets, and scripts used by the original skills.

books.description: Get independent reviews from three AI model providers and reconcile their findings.
Verify a change, get it reviewed, open and monitor its pull request, then merge when ready.
Prepare and verify a pull request through review and CI, leaving the merge to the developer.
Iterate on a change with a GPT Sol reviewer until both agents agree on the result.
